name: Insulin lispro
summary: A rapid-acting insulin analog that covers prandial glucose excursions with a fast onset, injected at or near mealtime.
mechanism: Reverses the B28/B29 amino acids of human insulin, reducing self-association into hexamers so the analog absorbs faster after subcutaneous injection.
pharmacodynamics: Mimics the physiologic prandial insulin peak; used with basal insulin for full coverage in type 1 and insulin-requiring type 2 diabetes.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Enzymatic degradation (insulin-degrading enzymes); hepatic and renal clearance

dosing.adult: Individualized; typically given within 15 minutes before or immediately after meals, as part of a basal-bolus or pump regimen

safety.pregnancy: Safe and standard; insulin is the preferred glucose-lowering treatment in pregnancy
safety.lactation: Generally safe; insulin does not cross into breast milk in significant amounts
warnings: Hypoglycemia, especially if meals are delayed or doses mismatched
Dose errors with concentrated U-200 formulation
safety.overdose: Hypoglycemia; treat with oral or IV glucose and close monitoring

clinicalPearls: Inject within 15 minutes of the meal — its window is narrow compared with regular insulin.
U-200 lispro is available for patients needing large doses; never confuse units with volume.
good: Fast onset allows flexible meal timing and tight postprandial control.
bad: Requires basal insulin to bridge gaps; hypoglycemia if meals are delayed after dosing.
